title: How to Move a 100-Ton Rock Without a Crane
lines: This rock weighs a hundred tons. His job? Move it. No crane.
He pushes. The rock doesn't even notice.
So he ties a rope and pulls. That rope is rated for two tons. The rock weighs fifty times more.
So he grabs a lever. Long side, short side: fifty to one.
He's too light, so he adds a ton of sandbags. And the edge lifts!
Now slide rollers underneath. He's not dragging a hundred tons anymore. He's rolling it. That only takes about two tons of pull.
A pry bar nudges it a few centimeters per heave. At this rate, it'll take a week.
So he builds a capstan. Long arms, skinny drum: twenty to one.
Loop the rope around a pulley on the rock, and that doubles it. One engineer, forty times stronger.
The rollers move at half the rock's speed, so it just keeps coming.
Destination reached. One guy, one rock, zero cranes.
